issue.body:
This logic was simply missing from the implementation. It's a pretty tricky case since it only reproduces with wrapped parsers but works fine when directly using `JsonXContentParser`.

Closes #111812.

body:
In #111937 I try to address this issue and add tests for both cases. But in the BigDecimal case now matter how large the number double is always found and precision is lost. I finally found the underlying Jackson issue:

We need to upgrade Jackson in order to gain access to a corrected `getNumberValueExact()` method. I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/111948 to upgrade.

issue.title: Handle BigInteger in xcontent copy

labels.name: auto-merge-without-approval
labels.description: Automatically merge pull request when CI checks pass (NB doesn't wait for reviews!)

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When xcontent is copied, the parse tree is walked and each element is passed to the given generator. In the case of numbers, BigInteger is currently not handled. Although arbitrary precision BigIntegers are not supported in Elasticsearch, they appear in xcontent when using unsigned long fields. This commit adds handling for that case, and also ensures all token types are handled. Note that BigDecimal are not supported at all since double is the largest floating point mapper supported.

closes #111812
